clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old woman presented with one month of progressive episodic memory deficit characterized by inability to remember events even minute-to-minute, marked impairment in remembering new information, and worsening during emotional distress. Neurologic examination revealed only episodic memory deficit without other focal signs. EEG showed temporal lobe epileptiform discharges without clinical seizures. Brain MRI revealed bilateral temporal lobe hyperintense lesions on FLAIR and T2-weighted images. CSF analysis showed mild pleocytosis and oligoclonal bands. She was treated with IV immunoglobulins 0.4 g/kg/d for 5 days and oral prednisone 25 mg/d, followed by a second course of IVIG at 3 months. By 7 months after onset, she demonstrated marked clinical improvement with MMSE score of 30/30, recovery of recent memory, and restoration of social functioning. Pelvic imaging was normal. The clinical presentation of isolated limbic encephalitis with memory impairment, characteristic EEG findings, inflammatory CSF with oligoclonal bands, bilateral temporal lobe MRI abnormalities, and robust response to immunotherapy are consistent with anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
